mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth (INDPRO > 1.5% monthly).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and reduced business investment, which correlates with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when consumer spending growth is above 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary policy tightening amid persistent inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is accelerating (>0.5% qoq).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both HOUST and GDPC1 for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in housing demand and overall economic activity, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both decline month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong labor market growth (>0.5% monthly payroll growth).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in PAYEMS growth above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating monthly change in INDPRO (i.e., month-over-month INDPRO growth increases from previous month) signals improving manufacturing momentum, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly growth accelerates (second derivative > 0) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when consumer confidence is falling sharply.
